record.paper_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For RIS-aided systems that use statistical channel state information and optimize long-term performance under infrequent RIS updates, what achievable-rate inner bounds can be derived for the ergodic-rate optimization problem, instead of relying only on outer bounds?

evidence.quote: In this area, there is a need for achievable rate (inner bound) expressions rather than outer bounds. Inner bounds for this expression have not been developed at the time of the writing of this paper.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-user MIMO communication system aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). Let the transmitter, receiver, and RIS be equipped with $N_t$, $N_r$, and $M$ antennas/elements, respectively. The received signal is
$$ y = (H_d + H_2 \, \Phi \, H_1)\, x + n, $$
where $H_d \in \mathbb{C}^{N_r \times N_t}$ is the direct channel, $H_1 \in \mathbb{C}^{M \times N_t}$ and $H_2 \in \mathbb{C}^{N_r \times M}$ are the transmitter–RIS and RIS–receiver channels, $\Phi = \mathrm{diag}(e^{j\theta_1},\dots,e^{j\theta_M})$ is the diagonal RIS phase-shift matrix with $\theta_m \in [0,2\pi)$, $x$ is the transmit signal with covariance $Q\succeq 0$, $\mathrm{tr}(Q)\le P$, and $n\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,\sigma^2 I)$.

Assume that the channels $H_d, H_1, H_2$ are random with a known joint distribution (statistical CSI), and that the RIS configuration $\Phi$ together with the input covariance $Q$ are chosen as functions of this distribution only (i.e., they are held fixed over the coherence horizon during which the instantaneous channels vary). Define the ergodic rate
$$ R(\Phi, Q) = \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \log\det\!\left( I + \tfrac{1}{\sigma^2}(H_d + H_2 \Phi H_1) Q (H_d + H_2 \Phi H_1)^H \right) \right], $$
with the ergodic-rate optimization problem
$$ R^\star = \sup_{\Phi,\, Q:\ \mathrm{tr}(Q)\le P} R(\Phi, Q). $$

Problem. Derive a closed-form achievable-rate inner bound $\underline{R}(\Phi,Q)$, satisfying $\underline{R}(\Phi,Q) \le R(\Phi,Q)$ for all feasible $(\Phi,Q)$, that depends only on the channel statistics (e.g., covariance matrices, line-of-sight components, Rician factors) and that can be used as a tractable surrogate objective for optimizing the long-term RIS configuration $\Phi$ and input covariance $Q$ when only statistical CSI is available. The bound should be tight enough to provide a meaningful guarantee on the achievable ergodic rate, and the resulting optimization should be amenable to practical algorithms.
artifact.status_search_result: Since 2023, several works have derived closed-form approximations and lower bounds on the ergodic rate of RIS-aided systems under statistical CSI using tools such as Jensen's inequality, majorization theory, and large-system/asymptotic analysis, including for single-RIS MISO, double-RIS MIMO with spatial correlation, and stacked intelligent metasurfaces. Many derive asymptotic or approximate ergodic-rate expressions rather than fully rigorous inner bounds, and general tight inner bounds for arbitrary correlated MIMO settings remain an active topic of research.

status_evidence.title: Achievable Rate Analysis and Optimization of Double-RIS Assisted Spatially Correlated MIMO with Statistical CSI
status_evidence.snippet: Derived asymptotic ergodic rate expressions and a full statistical CSI-enabled optimal design for double-RIS spatially correlated MIMO.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: closed-form asymptotic ergodic-rate inner approximations derived for double-RIS correlated MIMO.

status_evidence.title: RIS-Aided MISO Systems with Statistical CSI: Channel Estimation, Analysis and Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Closed-form expressions of the ergodic rate are derived for statistical-CSI based RIS beamforming in MISO systems.
status_evidence.claim: Inner-bound/closed-form ergodic-rate expressions exist for MISO RIS with statistical CSI.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic Achievable Rate Maximization of RIS-Assisted mmWave MIMO-OFDM
status_evidence.snippet: Approximations of the ergodic achievable rate derived via majorization theory and Jensen's inequality.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-bound approximations to the ergodic rate have been developed for RIS MIMO-OFDM.

status_evidence.title: Achievable Rate Optimization for Large Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces Based on Statistical CSI
status_evidence.snippet: Statistical CSI based achievable-rate optimization for stacked intelligent metasurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works extend statistical-CSI inner-bound optimization to multi-layer RIS architectures.
